summary: Wave 9 regression — Admin vendor invites, notice document uploads, Permissions Matrix and Committee external invitees. Backend: 13/13 pytest passing in /app/backend/tests/wave9_test.py. Frontend Playwright verified: PERMISSIONS tab appears in admin nav, 9 role rows render with per-cell perm-{role}-{action} testids, toggle→save→reload persistence WORKS (perm-legal_counsel-modify flipped True→False and survived a full page reload), Reset Defaults restores the matrix, Vendors tab shows vendor-invite-toggle → vendor-invite-form. Backend flows exercised end-to-end: invite → verify token GET → set-password → vendor login (200), one-time-use token rejected on reuse (404), registration template upload + public download with correct Content-Type, notice create + primary+attachment upload (persisted on GET /notices/{ref}/admin), reviewer role 403 blocked from POST /notices with 'Permissions Matrix' in error detail, committee external invitee create → public GET /committees/external/{token} returns tender snapshot → POST /decision flips status to 'accepted' in list_committees, invalid decision → 400.

critical.issue: Route ordering bug: vendor_invites.router was registered AFTER vendors.router, so vendors.py catch-all `GET /{vendor_ref}` (which requires admin auth) matched `/registration-template` first and returned 401 on the PUBLIC download endpoint. FIXED by moving vendor_invites.router include BEFORE vendors.router in server.py.

issues: Recurring React hydration warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option>. Same cosmetic dev-mode warning already flagged in iteration_16 — caused by ve-dynamic instrumentation wrapping option text. Not user-facing but pollutes console.

action_items: Route-ordering bug already fixed by testing agent — main agent should review /app/backend/server.py change (vendor_invites now included before vendors) and keep this ordering.
Consider fixing hydration warning by removing <span> children of <option> in AnalyticsPanel / other dropdowns (previously flagged in iter16, still present).
critical_code_review_comments: FastAPI route collision: any future router that uses the same /api/v1/vendors prefix must be included BEFORE vendors.router because `GET /{vendor_ref}` is a greedy catch-all with auth. Consider making vendor_ref match a stricter regex like `{vendor_ref:^PMC-SUP-[0-9]+$}` to eliminate this class of bug entirely.

routers/permissions.py — put_matrix accepts whatever row set the client sends without validating that all 9 default roles are still present. Combined with a stale/partial GET (or a UI that only re-sends visible rows), an admin can accidentally shrink the matrix to a subset — reproduced during this run against a curl-polluted DB (GET returned 2 rows).  Recommendation: server should merge posted rows on top of DEFAULT_MATRIX rather than replace outright.

routers/vendor_invites.invite_vendor — verify_url is built from config.FRONTEND_URL but also RETURNED to the admin in the API response; if FRONTEND_URL is misconfigured, admins may copy a broken link. Add a health check or fallback to request.headers.origin.

routers/committee.py — external_invitees accept_token is stored plaintext and never invalidated after decision. Anyone with the URL can flip 'accepted' → 'declined' repeatedly. Consider one-time use (unset token after first decision).

committee.external_invite_meta returns full invitee snapshot including email/designation without any rate-limit or token entropy check — token comes from new_magic_token() (fine) but there is no attempts throttle.

Server.py router order was changed by this testing iteration — vendor_invites now precedes vendors to fix a 401-on-public-download bug.
rca of the issue: Registration template download returned 401. Root cause: FastAPI evaluates routes in registration order across the whole app. vendors.py has `GET /api/v1/vendors/{vendor_ref}` (auth-gated). vendor_invites.py has `GET /api/v1/vendors/registration-template` (public). Because vendor_invites.router was registered AFTER vendors.router, the greedy `{vendor_ref}` route matched `registration-template` as if it were a vendor_ref, triggered `require_role('admin', 'reviewer')` and returned 401 without ever reaching the public handler. Verified via curl: GET returned 401 unauth. Mitigation applied: move `app.include_router(vendor_invites.router)` above `app.include_router(vendors.router)` in server.py; verified curl now returns 200 with the PDF bytes and the test suite is green.
